chapter: Original Dixieland Jazz Band: Chicago and New York
title: Shields leaves; Artie Seberg's clarinet tone and Albert system
summary: Shields goes back to New Orleans, Seberg replaces him at the Balconades, and Edwards praises Seberg and talks of Albert versus Boehm clarinet and the Dorseys.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: yes that's right you mentioned that and then uh after we left the Foley-Bergé we uh did some uh one night stands in Pennsylvania and Frankie Signorelli played those Henry only came to New York and worked at the Balconades Shields didn't wish to come to New York and he left the band returned to New Orleans and went to California I think where his wife was living and we got Artie Seberg Artie Seberg played his tone was almost like Shields it was difficult to tell them apart and he played all Shields uh style and parts in the recordings did Lytel ever play with the band? Lytel yes he did yes he played uh uh when we first went to the to uh the Balconades that was 19 19 1922 he followed him and then who followed him? Seberg, Artie Seberg Artie Seberg has since passed away he was a very fine clarinet player he was uh excellent musician I was surprised at him because I afterwards heard him play in the pit in uh Paramount Theater he did some condensors and he I sat near him his clarinet work was brilliant he had a beautiful tone he used an Albert system yeah clarinet usually they used Bayham system you see he transposed he was a thorough musician he read beautiful and his tone quality was nice and he had an excellent jazz tone because he was so full not loud and not high but it was like three clarinets wrapped up into one the tone quality was so big
I like that Albert system myself you do yes I think it has a better tone somehow

well there's a strange thing to tell me that uh Jimmy Darcy used to use half Albert and half Bayham system he was quite a clarinist I liked his work very much and Tommy could really play jazz although he didn't play too much of it except that later on all the bands the big bands and had a small combination a Dixaland combination in them and the men liked the Dixaland style worked so much that it would have to be uh five men playing and uh fifteen men clapping hands so the bosses come along and say well let's get rid of these fifteen other men we'll just engage the five
